voice: Kristen - Friendly Casual Conversation BFF (ElevenLabs, eleven_v4)
welcome: Hey, welcome to AI Activation, Customer Success Cohort 2. Here's how this works. For four weeks, Monday through Thursday, you get one short activity a day, fifteen to twenty minutes, and they all build toward Friday. Friday is where the week comes together, and it's the one you submit in the channel. You'll also pick a deeper path, a team capstone or a certification of your choice, and we'll help you finish it at the drop-in sessions. We pause for Thanksgiving week, then come back for two more weeks. One rule before you start: anything proprietary stays in Copilot, ACE, or SideKick. That's it. Come, learn, play, build, and share. See you in the channel.

weeks.w1: This week is about how you think with AI, not what you produce with it. Four moves: challenge your ideas, translate for different audiences, simplify without dumbing down, and reverse-engineer great prompts. Each day is twenty minutes. On Friday you'll bring all four into one messy, real situation. Don't overthink it. Just show up Monday with one rough idea.
weeks.w2: Week two points AI at data. You'll engineer a synthetic dataset on Monday, hunt its patterns on Tuesday, wire in real-world signals on Wednesday, and write an intelligence report on Thursday. Friday, you build a live dashboard that tells the whole story. If spreadsheets aren't your thing, even better. This week was built for you.
weeks.w3: This week is a complete product lifecycle in five days. Monday you design a CS process by hand, on paper. Tuesday, AI turns the sketch into a working app. Wednesday you polish and package it. Thursday you learn how GitHub works. And Friday, you ship it to a real, live URL. Every day has one job, and all five connect.
weeks.w4: Last week, and it's not a graduation, it's a launch. Monday and Tuesday, AI becomes your mirror and your map: what kind of AI thinker are you becoming, and what's next. Wednesday and Thursday, you design and build your own AI activation program for your team. Friday, you present it. Finish strong.

days.w1d1: Day one, and it starts with a habit flip. Most of us use AI to agree with us. Today, hand it your rough idea and ask it to attack. Find the weak spots, expose the assumptions, argue the other side as hard as it can. Push back where you disagree, and keep what survives. Maybe it's that onboarding change you've been mulling over. Let AI punch holes in it for ten minutes. When you're done, ask AI to write the decision log for you. Twenty minutes, one stronger idea.
days.w1d2: Today is about sequence. Before you write a single word, have AI profile your audience. A senior leader, a customer, and a technical reader all need to hear your idea differently. Ask what each one fears, what they want, and what loses them in ten seconds. Then let the profile drive the message, not your instinct. Try profiling all three in one prompt first. The differences will surprise you, and they'll do the positioning work for you.
days.w1d3: Analogies are today's tool. Take your idea, or any process you own, and have AI explain it through analogies for three different audiences. The goal is easier to understand without becoming wrong. And here's the move that matters: once you have your analogies, ask AI which of these could be misunderstood, and how. That one follow-up question is where the real refinement happens, and it basically writes your submission note for you.
days.w1d4: Today you think backwards. Find one great piece of output, a sharp executive summary, a clean QBR, anything you admire. Ask AI what prompt most likely created it, in four parts: role, context, format, and constraints. Then improve that prompt, and run it until the result beats the original. This is the foundation skill of everyone who uses AI at a high level, and after today, you can teach it to someone else.
days.w1d5: It's Friday, the week's synthesis. Bring one genuinely messy situation from your work. A relationship showing risk, an unclear leadership ask, a proposal with too many stakeholders. Start with a brain dump: paste everything you know in one go, and ask AI to structure what matters before you touch solutions. Then run the week's four moves: challenge, translate, simplify, reverse-engineer. Post your read, your recommendation, one stakeholder message, and an honest reflection on where AI helped, and where your judgment carried it.
days.w2d1: Today AI becomes a data engineer. Ask it to generate a realistic synthetic dataset from your world: health scores, renewals, ticket trends, whatever you know best. Don't stop at rows. Push it to build in patterns: regional trends, anomalies, correlations. Here's a good trick: have it hide one pattern you'd expect, and one that would surprise you. This dataset is the foundation for Friday's dashboard, so before you post it, ask AI what story the data tells.
days.w2d2: AI was built on pattern recognition, and today you point it at your data. Don't ask for a summary. Ask what's happening, how it got here, where it's concentrated, why it looks this way, and where it's heading if nothing changes. Then push harder: what would a skeptical CFO challenge? And when the analysis feels done, ask one more thing: what am I not asking that I should be? That question finds the best insight of the session, almost every time.
days.w2d3: Your data doesn't live in a vacuum. Today you feed AI outside signals, market shifts, industry news, competitor moves, and ask it to connect them to your dataset. Then project the future: what does this look like in twelve months if these forces continue? Ask for three future states, optimistic, pessimistic, and most likely. The gap between those three is where the strategic questions live, and it's exactly what Friday's dashboard needs.
days.w2d4: Today you write the brief a leader could act on. Four sections: what the data shows, the anomalies and hidden patterns, the key insights and why they matter, and the future-state argument from yesterday's work. After AI drafts each section, ask it one question: what's the single most important sentence here, and is it the most prominent? Making AI rank its own findings sharpens every section. The clearer this report, the stronger tomorrow's dashboard.
days.w2d5: Friday, the week's synthesis, and it all comes together. You have the data, the patterns, the outside signals, and the report. Now build the live dashboard that tells the story in one place. At least three chart types, a key insights panel, an anomalies callout, and a future-state section. Before you build, paste Thursday's report into AI and ask what this dashboard must communicate in the first ten seconds to a senior leader. Let that answer drive the layout. The bar: a CFO asks follow-up questions instead of dismissing it.
days.w3d1: No AI tools until the second half of today. Design a CS process from scratch, an onboarding flow, an escalation path, whatever you'd improve, and draw it by hand. Every stage, every decision point. Then photograph it, and hand the photo to an AI vision tool. Ask it to interpret the drawing, find the gaps, and write a one-page process brief. Analog first, AI second. That sequence beats a blank prompt every single time.
days.w3d2: Yesterday's sketch becomes software today. Feed the photo and the brief into an AI builder together, in one prompt: use the drawing as the structure and the brief as the content, and build an animated, interactive HTML app a colleague could click through in under three minutes. Don't accept the first result. Iterate until the flow matches your intent. You're about to build a working app without writing a line of code.
days.w3d3: A working app and a deployable app are two different things, and today you close the gap. Three jobs: polish anything that feels rough, have AI clean up the code, and decompose it into a proper package of separate files. Best prompt of the day: ask AI for three things that would confuse a first-time user, three things that look unpolished, and three structural improvements. It will find more than you would.
days.w3d4: Today is the quiet one. No building, just learning the place your work will live tomorrow. Watch the GitHub basics video linked on the card, about what repos are, and how commit, push, and pull work. No coding background needed. Take notes, and post one thing that surprised you, plus one question you still have. Tomorrow, the vocabulary pays off when you ship.
days.w3d5: Friday, the week's synthesis, and it's launch day. Create your GitHub account, make a public repository, upload Wednesday's package, and turn on GitHub Pages. That's it. You'll have a real URL for a tool you drew by hand on Monday. Before you post the link, open it on your phone and show someone outside the program. If they get it in thirty seconds, it's ready. Sketch to shipped in five days. That's a professional capability now.
days.w4d1: Today AI holds up a mirror. Pour the whole journey in: what clicked, what surprised you, what frustrated you, and be specific about the moments. Then ask for something most people never try: based on all this, what kind of AI thinker am I becoming, and which skills are emerging strongest? Don't give it the polished summary. Give it the raw version, including the activities you almost skipped. The more honest the input, the better the read.
days.w4d2: Yesterday was the mirror, today is the map. Have AI take your reflection and identify the two or three skills most worth polishing, then design an upskilling track built for your role, your gaps, and your ambitions. Push it further: what should someone on your trajectory be doing with AI six months from now that they aren't today? Then ask which single activity would create the most visible impact for your team fastest. Start there.
days.w4d3: You've lived this program from the inside. Today you design one from the outside. Sketch three or four themed tracks for your own sub-team: a clear theme, a weekly arc, and a few activities that build on each other. Use AI as your curriculum partner: have it challenge your ideas, fix the sequencing, and kill anything that's homework instead of learning. Start where your team actually is, not where you wish they were.
days.w4d4: Today the tracks become a program your team could start Monday. Name it, set the weekly themes, write the activity briefs, define the Friday challenges and what good submissions look like. Then pressure-test it: have AI role-play your most skeptical teammate. Busy, tried AI once, unimpressed. Ask where they'd check out, and fix those moments now. By the end of today, you're not a participant anymore. You're a program designer.
days.w4d5: The final Friday, and the moment it's all been building toward. Present your AI activation plan: what it achieves and for whom, your tracks and why you sequenced them that way, the activity you're proudest of, and your personal commitment going forward. One tip for the opening: start with the moment from these four weeks where AI genuinely surprised you. Not the best output. The moment something shifted. That's the story your audience will remember. Go finish strong.
